To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of MUC5A and MUC5B genes was detected in 7/15 primary breast tumor extracts and 9/46 bone marrow aspirate samples, respectively.

(i) MUC5B is a specific molecular marker for detection of bone marrow‐metastatic breast cancer cells; (ii) MUC5 mRNA expression is a useful marker for detection of disseminated breast cancer cells; and (iii) MUC5 and CK19 mRNA are the best molecular markers for detection of disseminative breast cancer cells.
MUC5 mRNA is a useful marker for breast cancer detection and its expression is associated with the dissemination of breast cancer cells to the bone marrow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an RT‐PCR method to detect disseminated breast cancer cells.
the use of a multimarker approach for detection of disseminated breast cancer cells.
the use of MUC5b gene expression as a molecular marker to detect disseminated breast cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of multimolecular marker approach could contribute to the detection of disseminated breast cancer cells in the peripheral blood and bone marrow, and could have a significant clinical impact in the follow‐up of breast cancer patients, especially in the early stages of the disease.
MUC5 mRNA is a specific marker applicable for the molecular diagnosis of bone marrow and blood disseminated breast cancer cells.
